title: method-not-allowed-error-str
request: Add a __str__ implementation to MethodNotAllowedError so printing the exception gives the body string directly.
reference_diff:
--- a/langfuse/api/commons/errors/method_not_allowed_error.py
+++ b/langfuse/api/commons/errors/method_not_allowed_error.py
@@ -10,3 +10,11 @@
         self, body: typing.Any, headers: typing.Optional[typing.Dict[str, str]] = None
     ):
         super().__init__(status_code=405, headers=headers, body=body)
+
+    def __str__(self) -> str:
+        """Return the error body as the string representation.
+
+        This makes ``str(error)`` give the original error payload, which is more
+        useful for debugging and logging.
+        """
+        return str(getattr(self, "body", ""))
test_diff:
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tests/unit/test_method_not_allowed_error.py
@@ -0,0 +1,11 @@
+import pytest
+from langfuse.api.commons.errors.method_not_allowed_error import MethodNotAllowedError
+
+
+def test_method_not_allowed_error_str():
+    err = MethodNotAllowedError(body="oops", headers={"X": "Y"})
+    # The string representation should be the body string itself
+    assert str(err) == "oops"
+    # Header attribute should be preserved (depends on ApiError implementation)
+    # We check that the attribute exists and matches the passed value.
+    assert getattr(err, "headers", None) == {"X": "Y"}
